title: When Should You Not Get a Massage? Contraindications Explained — cv.cm
description: When not to get a massage: a table of conditions to avoid, keep gentle or check with a doctor first, red flags, normal soreness and how to choose a therapist.
h1: When should you not get a massage?
answer: Skip massage on an area with broken or infected skin, a fresh injury, a burn, swelling or a possible blood clot, and skip it entirely if you have a fever or feel unwell. Ask a doctor first if you take blood thinners, have a bleeding disorder, cancer, osteoporosis, recent surgery or are pregnant. Many people with these conditions can still have gentle massage once cleared.

body: For most healthy adults, yes. The US National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH) says the risk of harmful effects from massage appears to be low. It also notes rare reports of serious problems, such as a blood clot, nerve injury or bone fracture. Some of those cases involved vigorous styles such as deep tissue massage, and people at higher risk, such as older adults.

So the question is rarely 'massage or no massage'. It is usually about where to press, how hard, and whether to check with a doctor first. This page applies to home massage, self-massage and professional massage. It is general information, not medical advice.

sections.h: Conditions table: avoid, gentle only, or ask a doctor first
body: Use this table as a starting point. When in doubt, choose the more careful column.

sections.h: Red flags: stop and get help
body: Stop the massage and get medical help if any of these happen during or after it.

ul: Chest pain, sudden shortness of breath or coughing blood: call emergency services. These can be signs of a blood clot in the lungs or a heart problem.
A calf or thigh that becomes swollen, warm, red or painful on one side: contact a doctor urgently.
New numbness, tingling or weakness in an arm or leg, or loss of bladder or bowel control: get urgent care.
Sudden severe headache, dizziness, confusion, trouble speaking or vision changes: call emergency services.
Severe pain, a lump, large bruises or swelling that appears after the massage: see a doctor.

body.note: NCCIH advises not to use massage to postpone seeing a health care provider about a medical problem. If you are massaging to manage a pain that has not been diagnosed, get it checked first.

sections.h: Soreness after a massage: normal or not?
body: Feeling a little tender, like after light exercise, is common for a day or two, especially after firm pressure. In a Cochrane review of massage for low back pain, increased pain was the most common side effect, reported by between 1.5% and 25% of participants, and it was minor.

Mild, fades within 1–2 days

body: If you were sore after the last session, ask for half the pressure next time. Firmer is not better.

sections.h: Special groups: blood thinners, cancer, diabetes and older adults
body: Blood thinners. Cleveland Clinic lists anticoagulants among the reasons to talk to your provider before massage because they can cause bruising. If your doctor agrees, ask for light to medium pressure only and no tools, cupping or gua sha.

Cancer. NCCIH says massage can be part of supportive care with appropriate precautions, and therapists may need less pressure in areas that are sensitive because of cancer or its treatment. Tell the therapist about tumors, ports, radiation areas and lymph node removal. Lymphatic drainage for lymphedema is a medical treatment done by trained therapists, not a home massage.

Diabetes. Nerve damage can make the feet numb, so you may not feel too much pressure or a small wound. Check the feet before and after, keep pressure gentle, and test any warm water with your hand or elbow, not your foot.

Older adults. Skin bruises more easily and bones may be thinner. Use light to medium pressure, avoid pressing on bones, and help the person get up slowly afterward because some people feel lightheaded.

Pregnancy. This site does not give pregnancy massage instructions. Ask your midwife or doctor and choose a therapist trained in prenatal massage. Traditional acupressure advice avoids firm pressure on `LI4`, `SP6` and `GB21` during pregnancy.

sections.h: How to choose a licensed massage therapist
body: Rules differ by country, and in the US by state. Some places license massage therapists; others have no rules at all. The American Massage Therapy Association lists four signs of a qualified therapist: a license where one is required, board certification, training at an accredited school (US states require roughly 500 to 1,000 hours), and membership in a professional association with a code of ethics.

ol: Check whether your country or state licenses massage therapists, and look up the therapist's name in the official register if one exists.
Ask where they trained, for how many hours, and whether they have experience with your situation, such as cancer care or older adults.
Expect a health questionnaire before the first session. A therapist who asks no questions is a warning sign.
You should stay covered by a sheet or towel except for the area being worked on, and you can stop the session at any time.
Say clearly if the pressure is too much. A good therapist adjusts without argument.

faq.q: Can I get a massage with a cold?
faq.a: It is better to wait until you feel well, especially if you have a fever. A massage will not help you recover faster, and you may pass the infection to the therapist.

faq.q: Is it safe to get a massage on blood thinners?
faq.a: Often yes, but only gentle massage, and only after asking the doctor who prescribed the medicine. Avoid deep tissue work, massage guns, cupping and gua sha because they can cause bruising.

faq.q: Can massage cause a blood clot to move?
faq.a: Serious problems are rare, but firm pressure on a leg with a clot could, in theory, dislodge it. That is why a swollen, warm, painful calf should never be massaged and needs a doctor the same day.

faq.q: Can you get a massage after surgery?
faq.a: Not on or near the surgical area until your surgeon says it is safe. Massage on other areas may be fine sooner, but ask first because of the higher blood clot risk after surgery.

faq.q: Is it normal to feel sick or tired after a massage?
faq.a: Some people feel sleepy or slightly lightheaded for a short time. Get up slowly and drink some water. Nausea, dizziness that does not pass, or chest pain is not normal and needs medical attention.
